title: Manufacturing Security Lead
descriptionHtml:
We’re a team of experts pushing the limits of what’s possible, united by our common goal to unlock true freedom through digital ownership, making technology accessible for all. We believe in a world where users, creators and enterprises manage their value with ownership and freedom. Our curiosity drives us to innovate, empowering individuals on a global scale. We believe change is constant and our team moves forward as one, with a culture of problem-solving where every employee is empowered and supported to challenge tradition and create solutions. Our mission is simple: to make self-custody accessible and give people the keys to their own financial futures. If you want to make a true impact, we want you to join us at Ledger.

At Ledger, we’re proud to be the global platform for digital assets and Web3, with over 20% of the world’s crypto assets secured through our Ledger devices. With our headquarters in Paris, and offices in Vierzon, Grenoble, Montpellier, London, Portland, Geneva, Zurich and Central Singapore, we have a team of around 600 professionals developing a variety of products and services to enable individuals and companies to securely buy, store, swap, grow and manage crypto assets – including the Ledger hardware wallets line with more than 7.5 millions units already sold in 200 countries.

 

The team:

Directly reporting to the Head of Physical Security, you'll own the security of Ledger's hardware manufacturing and supply chain, from components to finished devices, working with Operations, our contract manufacturers and specialist product-security teams

 

What you’ll be doing:

  • Define and maintain security requirements for manufacturing lines, suppliers and production changes.

  • Protect the exchange and integrity of sensitive manufacturing documentation, firmware and production artifacts, with strong supplier identity and authorisation.

  • Run component provenance checks, lot sampling and inspection, and the security gates of each production run.

  • Plan and run supplier and manufacturing-site assessments together with Physical Security.

  • Coordinate hardware tampering and supply-chain attack tests with Ledger's Donjon team and offensive-security specialists.

  • Set indicators and escalation thresholds, and coordinate investigations when something looks wrong.

  • Report progress and remaining exposure to security leadership.

  • Build and lead the manufacturing security team, and own its strategy, roadmap and budget.

  • Represent manufacturing security to Ledger's executives and to the leadership of our contract manufacturers and key suppliers.

 

What we’re looking for:

  • 10+ years in hardware, electronics or manufacturing security, including 5+ years leading a function or a supplier security programme.

  • Director-level management experience: you have built and led a security team, owned its budget and supplier relationships, and reported to executives.

  • Experience with hardware products built by contract manufacturers.

  • You have found or prevented a real tampering, counterfeit or manufacturing-integrity case.

  • You have run supplier and manufacturing-site assessments and worked directly with engineering and production teams.

  • Knowledge of supply-chain security frameworks such as NIST SP 800-161 and ISO 28000.

  • Fluent English.

 

At Ledger, we are dedicated to continually investing in our employees which is why we offer more than just salaries; we provide comprehensive compensation packages that include a wide range of benefits. Here are some of the benefits you can look forward to:

  • Flexible work options - Our hybrid policy allows employees to work from home up to 3 times per week

  • Health & Wellness support - Health and Life Insurance.

  • Financial growth opportunities - Employees can become shareholders in Ledger as well as other financial benefits depending on your country of work.

  • Commuter allowance - Ledger offers a commuter allowance to contribute to your preferred means of transportation.

  • Learning & Development - A comprehensive suite of training solutions providing a personalised learning experience for every employee.

For regionally specific benefits, your Talent Acquisition contact will be able to provide you with more information.

 

We’re committed to building an inclusive hiring process. If you need any adjustments or accommodations, just let us know, we’ll do our best to support you.

title: Marketing Generalist (Brand, Events & Partnerships)
descriptionHtml:
About Atira

Atira builds the commercial brain for industrials. Our agents 10x the sales engineers of today by offering the complete toolbox of tasks needed in complex environments. They handle everything from extracting and classifying requirements from incoming RFQs, orchestrating communication and information retrieval across multiple stakeholders and systems, while generating outcomes like documentation, production system inputs, or configuration recommendations. CRM. Atira. ERP.

We are one of the fastest growing teams in Munich and are looking for you to join us!

 

Why this role is a blank canvas

Brand is the one asset that compounds while everything else at a startup resets. Every deck, every customer story, every post builds on the last one, and the person who builds that foundation owns something no later hire can claim.

You will be one of the first people on our GTM team and the owner of how Atira looks, sounds, and gets found: our positioning, our visual identity, our customer stories, and our presence in a market where no one has built a great brand yet. You work directly with the founders and the GTM team who stay hands-on with positioning while you turn it into something the whole company builds on. And you won't start from zero: you'll build on our recently completed rebranding with a top-tier design agency and turn the new identity into everything Atira ships.

You won't be someone who "supports marketing" at Atira. You'll build and develop the company's brand in one of the hardest, most valuable B2B markets there is.

 

How the role sits in the team

You are the first person at Atira whose full-time job is creative marketing, working alongside Caro (Brand & Partnerships) as your day-to-day guide. You shape how Atira shows up in the world, and you make it happen yourself.

The role sits at the heart of our GTM team with our BDR, AE and GTM Engineer, and you work across every department: sales needs decks that make the product click, engineering needs a voice for what they build, product needs launches told in buyer language, recruiting needs a brand worth joining. You are the connective tissue that makes all of it look, feel and sound like one company.

This is a role for someone who loves the creative process and getting things done. You bring the ideas, shape the creative direction and own the execution: from the first concept to the final asset to the results. Whether it’s a campaign that gets the industry talking or an event that brings the right people together, your name is on it.

 

What you will do

You will shape how Atira looks, sounds and shows up in the world, and own the execution end to end: from the first concept to the final asset to the results. Concretely:

  • Turn ideas into campaigns. Develop concepts, bring them to life across channels and own the full cycle: strategy, setup, running and measuring. Success shows in inbound leads, engagement from ICP accounts and event leads

  • Tell stories that make industrial AI click. Write LinkedIn posts, website copy, newsletters, customer stories and articles that make complex topics interesting, accessible and impossible to ignore

  • Create the assets yourself. Build slides, sales decks, social visuals, videos, graphics and event material with tools like Figma, Canva, Adobe and CapCut. All built on Atira’s new brand guidelines

  • Shape our creative direction. Bring fresh ideas to the table, apply the design system across every touchpoint and help evolve it

  • Bring Atira into the rooms that matter. Own event concepts and preparation, from booth design to presentations and merchandise. Support on-site and drive the follow-up

  • Grow our channels and community. Run email campaigns, social media, PR and media outreach to reach the right people in our ICP

  • Learn what works. Track performance, understand what resonates and turn insights into better ideas

 

What we are looking for

Creativity, hunger, structure, and the kind of taste that makes Atira iconic. We care more about who you are than about your CV. We have hired strong people from non-traditional backgrounds before and will confidently do it again.

That said, here is what we typically see in strong candidates:

Your profile

  • Demonstrated ownership and initiative: a company you started, a leading role in a student initiative, an open-source project, a serious side build, or a role where you owned an outcome others would have delegated

  • You’ve optimized your AI tooling: you’ve invested heavily in building the skills and context layer to get the maximum out of your day

  • Genuine curiosity about manufacturing and industrials. You do not need to know everything on day one, but you need to be the kind of person who will know in week three

  • Full working proficiency in both German and English

  • Craft. Your portfolio shows crisp writing and strong visual judgment. At Atira we highly value people who have clear opinions and are not afraid to share them!

  • Start-up experience preferred

 

What you'll get

  • Validated traction. Leading Industrial customers including several with revenues above €1B within a clearly defined ICP. You are not hunting in the dark

  • Competitive salary & equity package and additional benefits including Wellpass, JobRad and company dinners

  • Most importantly: Collaborate & thrive in a high-performing but caring culture. We will own the industrial sales function but will do so with modesty and integrity

 

What success looks like after a few months

  • Atira has a positioning and messaging foundation adopted company-wide, a deck and template system every team actually uses, and a refreshed look that reflects it

  • One successful campaign end to end with evaluation.

  • Target buyers recognize us: growing LinkedIn engagement from ICP accounts, 2-3 published customer stories, presence at a key industry event, and the first inbound leads traceable to your work

  • One fair or event that you co-shaped.

title: Mobile UI Designer
descriptionHtml:

Design Stack

The Kind of Builder We Want

title: Montu Pharmacy Assessment Centre
descriptionHtml:
Ready to start or take the next step in your pharmacy career?

At Montu, we are doing things differently, and that includes how we recruit.

We are growing, and we are looking for enthusiastic, hardworking and patient-focused individuals to join our pharmacy team in Winnersh Triangle.

Whether you are looking to take your first step into healthcare, explore a new career in pharmacy or bring your existing pharmacy experience to a rapidly growing organisation, we would love to meet you.

We are hosting a Pharmacy Assessment Centre on Wednesday 18th November, giving you the opportunity to experience a different approach to recruitment, demonstrate your skills and learn more about what it is like to work at Montu.

You do not need previous pharmacy experience for all of our opportunities. For our entry-level positions, what matters most is your attitude, willingness to learn and genuine commitment to making a difference to patients.

Our pharmacy is busy. Really busy. It is a lively, energetic environment where things move quickly, teamwork is essential and no two days are quite the same. If you enjoy being on your feet, working alongside others and being part of a team where everyone has a role to play, you could feel right at home.

Behind every prescription we process is a patient relying on us to get things right. Whether you are packing medication, dispensing prescriptions or completing final accuracy checks, your contribution matters.

Opportunities Available

We are recruiting across several positions within our pharmacy team, with opportunities for both experienced pharmacy professionals and individuals looking to enter the industry.

Pharmacy Assistant

An excellent entry point into the pharmacy sector, with no previous pharmacy experience required.

You will support the day-to-day operations of our busy pharmacy, including preparing orders, packing medication, supporting stock management and helping ensure prescriptions are processed accurately and efficiently.

We are looking for individuals who are organised, reliable, comfortable with repetitive tasks and enjoy working in a hands-on, fast-paced environment.

Trainee Pharmacy Dispenser

Looking to develop a career in pharmacy? This could be your opportunity.

No previous dispensing experience is required. You will receive training and support as you develop the knowledge and practical skills needed to work within our dispensing team.

You will learn about prescription processing, medication handling, accuracy, pharmacy procedures and the importance of maintaining high standards of patient safety.

Pharmacy Dispenser

For individuals with an existing dispensing qualification and experience working within a pharmacy environment.

You will support the safe and accurate dispensing of prescriptions, working closely with pharmacists, technicians and the wider pharmacy team.

You will need excellent attention to detail, a strong understanding of pharmacy procedures and the ability to maintain accuracy while managing high prescription volumes.

Accuracy Checking Dispenser

We are looking for qualified and experienced Accuracy Checking Dispensers who can help maintain the high standards of accuracy and patient safety expected within our pharmacy.

You will undertake accuracy checking duties within the scope of your qualification, training and authorisation, supporting the efficient processing of prescriptions and working collaboratively with the wider team.

Accuracy Checking Technician (ACT)

For qualified Pharmacy Technicians with an accredited accuracy checking qualification and current GPhC registration.

You will play an important role in maintaining dispensing accuracy, supporting pharmacy operations and ensuring our processes meet the required professional and regulatory standards.

You will bring confidence, attention to detail and the ability to work effectively in a high-volume dispensing environment.

What Is Our Pharmacy Assessment Centre?

We know that traditional interviews do not always give people the best opportunity to demonstrate what they can do.

That is why we are taking a slightly different approach.

Our Pharmacy Assessment Centre is designed to be an engaging, practical and interactive experience where you can demonstrate your abilities, meet members of the Montu team and gain a better understanding of our working environment.

You can expect a combination of practical and team-based activities designed to assess skills relevant to working within our pharmacy, including:

  • Attention to detail and accuracy

  • Literacy and the ability to follow written instructions

  • Working effectively with others

  • Organisation and the ability to follow processes

  • Speed and efficiency without compromising accuracy

  • Communication and problem-solving

We are not expecting everyone to arrive with pharmacy knowledge, particularly those applying for our entry-level opportunities.

We are interested in how you approach tasks, how you work with others and whether you have the right attitude to succeed in our environment.

What happens after the assessment centre?

Candidates who successfully complete the assessment centre will be invited to attend a further on-site interview at Montu on a later date.

Please note that attendance at the assessment centre does not guarantee an interview or offer of employment.

What Are We Looking For?

We are looking for people who genuinely want to be part of a team making a difference.

Our ideal candidates will be:

  • Patient-focused: You understand that the work you do has a direct impact on the people relying on our service.

  • Detail-oriented: Accuracy matters, particularly when working with medication.

  • Comfortable in a busy environment: You enjoy an energetic workplace and can remain focused when things get hectic.

  • Reliable and hardworking: You take pride in doing your job well and supporting the people around you.

  • Team players: You understand that pharmacy operations depend on people working together.

  • Adaptable: You are comfortable learning new processes and responding to change.

  • Eager to learn: Whether you are new to pharmacy or already experienced, you are motivated to develop your skills.

You do not need to be the loudest person in the room or have years of experience to succeed here.

What matters is your work ethic, your attention to detail and your commitment to doing things properly.

About Montu

Montu is a leading medical cannabis company working to improve access to cannabis-based medicines for patients across the UK.

Through our specialist clinical services and pharmacy operations, we support patients receiving prescribed cannabis-based medicines for a range of eligible medical conditions.

Our multidisciplinary teams bring together clinicians, pharmacists, pharmacy technicians, dispensers and operational colleagues, all working towards the same goal: delivering safe, effective and patient-centred care.

We are a rapidly growing organisation, and our pharmacy is at the heart of what we do.

Every prescription represents a patient who is depending on us. From the moment a prescription reaches our pharmacy to the moment medication is dispatched, every member of our team plays an important role in that patient journey.

We are proud to be helping shape an evolving area of healthcare, and we want people who are excited to be part of that journey.

Why Join Montu?

Joining Montu means becoming part of a growing organisation where your work has purpose and your contribution makes a difference.

We offer:

  • Competitive salaries dependent on the position, qualifications and experience

  • Opportunities for training and professional development

  • Career progression within our growing pharmacy operations

  • A supportive and collaborative team environment

  • The opportunity to gain experience within a specialist area of healthcare

  • The chance to be part of a growing business helping improve patient access to prescribed medication

Further information about the benefits applicable to each role will be provided during the recruitment process.

Ready to Join Us?

Assessment Centre: Monday 2 November 2026

Location: Winnersh Triangle, Berkshire

If you are looking for an opportunity to begin a career in pharmacy, develop your existing skills or take the next step within a growing healthcare organisation, we would love to hear from you.

Apply now to be considered for a place at our Pharmacy Assessment Centre.

Following an initial review of applications, shortlisted candidates will receive further information about the assessment centre, including timings, location details and what to expect on the day.

title: Office Manager
descriptionHtml:
Office Manager

About us

Foundational is building the most precise picture of Earth and orbit, using lasers fired from the ground. We call it ground truth for orbit.

We design and run low-cost, autonomous satellite laser ranging stations. They measure the distance to satellites with extreme precision, day and night. Our data platform turns those measurements into tracking data and orbit products for satellite operators, space agencies and governments. We also build our own flight-proven laser retroreflector arrays, so any satellite can be tracked.

Our station network is expanding across continents. The data supports resilient navigation, Earth observation and the safe, sustainable use of space.

title: Operations Associate - Graduate Internship - November start
descriptionHtml:
Note: Partly is headquartered in Austin, TX with offices in London, UK, Christchurch, NZ and Auckland, NZ. Wherever you're based, we'll connect you with your nearest office for onboarding, and fly you to join the full team for our quarterly "Season Openers" (we cover travel and accommodation). If you're relocating to join us, we can also assist with relocation costs.


🚀 Our Story

Partly is building the infrastructure for anyone to repair anything. We believe everything built should be repairable, and we're building frontier AI to put repair knowledge to work, starting with the $2tn automotive market.

Our model, Interpreter, is the first AI purpose-built to understand repair. Trained on 1M+ car models and 1B+ parts, it reads a repair job the way an estimator does, resolves damage into the exact purchasable part, and shows its reasoning with a confidence score. On real production jobs, an estimator working with Interpreter reaches 98.8% parts-list accuracy, against 92.1% with today's tools. It powers PartlyRepair, used by collision shops, workshops and suppliers to take the admin off the job; PartlyLabs, the agentic infrastructure enterprises use to deploy Interpreter across their own workflows; and a developer API.

Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we've raised a $50m Series B led by DST Global (Anthropic, Airbnb, Meta, TikTok, Spotify), with Blackbird Ventures, WNDR, Activant Capital, Icehouse Ventures, Square Peg, Airtree and Ecliptic Venture Capital. Hear it from the team: Why Partly exists and AI at Partly.

🖍️ This role

As the first time was a huge success, we're launching version 2 of Partly's Repairer Ambassador Programme — a 3-month, full-time (with flexibility), paid internship for a small cohort of sharp, driven graduates who want real responsibility from day one. This is for people who want something more than a coffee run and a PowerPoint, and will lead to a full-time role for those who make a genuine impact.

Your job is simple: get newly onboarded repair shops actively using the Partly platform as quickly as possible. That means building relationships on the ground, understanding why certain shops aren't placing orders through us, and removing those barriers. You'll become the human face of Partly in repair shops across the UK — someone repairers genuinely trust and enjoy working with.

This is not a desk job. You'll spend your first 1–2 weeks in our London office receiving structured training before heading out to visit customers across your assigned region.

Key details:

  • Contract: 3 months, full-time with flexibility

  • Start: As soon as possible - November 2026

  • Location: UK-wide (field-based, with initial training in London)

💻 What will you do

  • Visit newly signed repair shops across your region and help them get up and running on the Partly platform.

  • Understand why shops aren't placing jobs through Partly and identify practical ways to remove those barriers.

  • Help repairers optimise and streamline their parts procurement workflows.

  • Track repairer activity, monitor adoption, and report insights back to the team on what's working and what isn't.

  • Build authentic, long-term relationships with shop owners and parts managers.

  • Feed customer insights back to the wider business so we can continually improve the product and onboarding experience.

🥷 What we're looking for

  • A recent graduate (university, HND, engineering course, or apprenticeship) with a genuine hunger to learn and get stuck in.

  • Strong common sense and the ability to read a room. This role is all about building trust with people who work with their hands for a living.

  • A full UK driving licence (having your own car is a strong advantage).

  • Comfortable spending most of the week on the road visiting customers.

  • Organised, self-directed, and confident working independently.

  • Comfortable around automotive professionals. This could come from a genuine interest in cars, working on your own vehicle, following motorsport, spending time in automotive environments, or simply having the curiosity and confidence to quickly learn the industry's language and "talk shop" with customers.

🪅 What You’ll Get

  • £102 per day

  • Travel and accommodation costs covered

  • Real responsibility and customer-facing experience from week one

  • A strong reference and genuine insight into how a fast-growing tech company operates

  • A realistic path to a full-time role at Partly at the end of the programme for the people who excel

So arbeitest du

title: Platform Engineer
descriptionHtml:
About us

At Trainline, our purpose is to empower greener travel choices, connecting people and places. Trainline enables millions of travellers to find and book the best value tickets across carriers, fares, and journey options through our highly rated mobile app, website, and B2B partner channels. 

Great journeys start with Trainline 🚄 

We’re Europe’s leading independent rail platform, helping millions of travellers find and book the best-value rail and coach journeys across our app, website and partner channels.

Our job is to make the green travel choice the best choice. By building a better train travel experience, we help more people choose rail - creating a positive impact for customers, our business and the planet.

We’re a team of more than 1,000 Trainliners from over 50 nationalities, working across London, Paris, Barcelona, Milan, Edinburgh and Madrid. Now is a brilliant time to join us and help shape the future of travel.

Introducing the Trainline Infrastructure Engineering and Tooling Team 👋

The Infrastructure Engineering and Tooling team, also known as Atlas, owns the ecosystem we use to deploy, run and manage services across the Trainline platform. Our work helps engineering teams across the business ship changes safely and confidently, so millions of travellers can rely on Trainline every day.

You'll join a collaborative team of software and platform engineers at all levels of experience. We work across Terraform, AWS, Node.js, C# and Python, and we don't expect you to know it all from day one. You'll work closely with engineers, Tech Leads and Engineering Managers, with support from a Senior Principal Engineer and the Head of Engineering, to improve our platform and deliver meaningful infrastructure change.

In this role as the Platform Engineer, you will...🚄

  • Contribute to improvements across Trainline's engineering platforms, building scalable, reliable and secure infrastructure that supports teams across the business.

  • Implement infrastructure changes with Terraform, following existing module patterns and suggesting ideas to improve quality, maintainability and automation.

  • Apply least-privilege and secure-by-default principles across our AWS accounts, helping our infrastructure meet Trainline's standards for security and operational excellence.

  • Build and improve automation, services and tooling in Node.js or Python to make delivery faster, safer and more repeatable.

  • Learn and grow with your colleagues through code reviews, pairing and shared knowledge, giving and receiving constructive feedback along the way.

  • Work with Tech Leads, Delivery Managers and cross-functional colleagues to understand priorities, plan your work and manage dependencies.

  • Raise risks, blockers and questions early, helping the team keep delivery moving at a sustainable pace.

  • Test, validate and deploy infrastructure changes through CI/CD (continuous integration and continuous delivery) pipelines, making sure they are robust, well documented and ready for production.

We'd love to hear from you if you have...🔍

  • Professional experience as a software engineer, writing code in Python, Node.js, C# or a similar programming language.

  • An understanding of software engineering best practice, with a focus on writing clean, maintainable and testable code.

  • Experience with AWS services such as ECS, Lambda, CloudFront, IAM and S3, following operational and security best practice.

  • Experience delivering infrastructure with Terraform or another infrastructure as code tool.

  • An understanding of DevOps practices and CI/CD, for example using GitHub Actions.

  • Experience using AI tooling in your day-to-day work, for example for coding, code review, research and productivity.

  • A curious mindset and the ability to pick up new technologies quickly and apply them well.

More information:

Enjoy fantastic perks like private healthcare & dental insurance, a generous work from abroad policy, 2-for-1 share purchase plans, an EV Scheme to further reduce carbon emissions, extra festive time off, and excellent family-friendly benefits. 

We prioritise career growth with clear career paths, transparent pay bands, personal learning budgets, and regular learning days. Jump on board and supercharge your career from day one! 

We're operating a hybrid model and ask that Trainliners work from the office a minimum of 60% of their time over a 12-week period. We also have a 28-day Work from Abroad policy.

Our values represent the things that matter most to us and what we live and breathe everyday, in everything we do: 

  • 💭 Think Big - We're building the future of rail 

  • ✔️ Own It - We focus on every customer, partner and journey 

  • 🤝  Travel Together - We're one team 

  • ♻️ Do Good - We make a positive impact 

We know that having a diverse team makes us better and helps us succeed. And we mean all forms of diversity - gender, ethnicity, sexuality, disability, nationality and diversity of thought. That's why we're committed to creating inclusive places to work, where everyone belongs and differences are valued and celebrated.

Interested in finding out more about what it's like to work at Trainline? Why not check us out on LinkedIn, Instagram and Glassdoor!

title: Platform Software Engineer
descriptionHtml:
The Developer Enablement & Security (DE&S) team within Platform Engineering owns the tooling that TomTom engineers use to write, build, store and secure code. This covers GitHub platform management, artifact management with JFrog Artifactory, security scanning, developer tooling and AI governance platforms. We treat internal developers as our customers and aim to make the secure path the easy path.


What you will do

  • Administer and automate GitHub Enterprise: repository settings, rulesets, access and governance across a large repository estate.

  • Operate and improve JFrog Artifactory, including repository configuration, cleanup, permissions and support for our hybrid cloud setup.

  • Replace repetitive admin work with scripts and automation using Python, Bash and REST APIs.

  • Build and maintain GitHub Actions workflows and support teams whose pipelines pull and publish packages.

  • Manage platform configuration as code with Terraform or similar tools.

  • Use AI tools to speed up automation and support work, and help developers adopt them safely in line with our AI governance approach.

  • Take ownership of well-defined platform tasks from start to finish, asking for guidance when needed.

  • Troubleshoot developer issues across DNS, TLS, proxies and authentication.

  • Write and maintain documentation and runbooks that let developers help themselves.

  • Explain platform policies clearly and work with developers to adopt them.


What you need

  • 2 to 5 years of experience in DevOps, platform, build or infrastructure engineering.

  • Git and GitHub: comfortable with branching, pull requests, reviews and repository settings; hands-on experience with GitHub Actions.

  • Scripting and automation: Python or Bash, with experience calling REST APIs.

  • CI/CD basics: you have built or maintained pipelines and understand how builds pull and publish packages.

  • Package ecosystems: working knowledge of at least two of Maven/Gradle, npm, PyPI, Docker and NuGet.

  • Linux and networking: you can find your way around a server and troubleshoot DNS, TLS, proxy and authentication problems.

  • Infrastructure as Code: some experience with Terraform or a similar tool, ideally for managing platform configuration.

  • AI in day-to-day work: good understanding of AI coding assistants and agents such as GitHub Copilot or Claude, and hands-on experience using them to write scripts, automate tasks, troubleshoot and document your work.


Nice to have
  • Cloud basics in Azure or AWS.

  • Identity basics: exposure to SSO, SAML/OIDC or SCIM.

  • Security awareness: secrets management, least privilege and dependency scanning; exposure to Black Duck, Coverity or Veracode is a plus.

  • Admin experience on a developer platform such as GitHub, GitLab, Artifactory, Nexus or Jenkins.


    • How you work
  • You write clear docs and runbooks, because platform teams depend on them.

  • You treat internal developers as customers and can explain a policy without creating friction.

  • You keep learning; you pick up new tools quickly rather than relying on knowing one specific product.

title: Pre-Sales Engineer
descriptionHtml:
Location: London or Bristol, UK (hybrid, three days a week in the office)

Level: Senior Engineer C3

Team: Growth

Salary: £65,000 - £75,000 + discretionary bonus

Contract: Permanent

Reporting To: Head of Sales Engineering

Please note: This role requires an existing right to work in the UK. We can’t offer visa sponsorship, but we review sponsorship role by role, so keep an eye on our careers site for future opportunities.


About Kaluza

Kaluza is the Energy Intelligence Platform, turning energy complexity into seamless coordination. We help energy companies overcome today’s challenges while accelerating the shift to a clean, electrified future.

Our platform orchestrates millions of real-time decisions across homes, devices, markets and grids. By combining predictive algorithms with human-centred design, Kaluza makes clean energy dependable, affordable and adaptive to everyday life.

With teams across Europe, Asia and Australia, and a joint venture with Mitsubishi Corporation in Japan, we power leading companies including OVO, AGL and ENGIE, as well as innovators like Volvo and Volkswagen.


What you’ll do

As a Pre-Sales Engineer, you are a trusted technical contributor within our team, helping deliver impactful sales engagements through configuration and development in our demo environments. You’ll play a contributor role to larger deals, and often lead pre-sales activities for smaller or less complex opportunities. You are a key part of the commercial engine, helping us scale by ensuring our technical pre-sales efforts are thorough, accurate, and client-focused.

This role will report to the Head of Sales Engineering and you’ll be part of a team that works on sales to Kaluza’s largest clients globally. You will have broad expertise on Kaluza’s product suite and our value differentiators and will develop depth in particular areas of our products. You will have a good understanding of the challenges facing energy retailers from a client or user perspective and be able to show-case how our solutions solve them.. 

You will play a crucial role in building product demonstrations and collateral that evangelises the Kaluza platform.

  • Own and deliver demo activities for small to mid-size opportunities, especially during high team capacity periods. This includes configuring and delivering tailored product demonstrations and responding to client technical questions with clarity and confidence.

  • Support technical delivery on complex deals, working alongside senior team members to prepare solution configurations, contribute to discovery conversations, and ensure client requirements are well captured and translated.

  • Collaborate closely with Sales, Product, and Engineering teams to scope solutions, validate feasibility, and communicate trade-offs in a clear and client-friendly manner.

  • Lead or contribute to proof-of-concept (PoC) projects, ensuring they reflect client needs and demonstrate our platform’s ability to deliver measurable outcomes. Track PoC success criteria and highlight risks or gaps to the wider team.

  • Represent the Pre-Sales function in internal planning and alignment sessions, helping ensure technical accuracy, smooth handovers, and clear documentation for post-sale teams.

  • Document and share learnings from client engagements, including product feedback, recurring questions, and potential areas for improvement in our pre-sales approach or demo assets.


What you’ll bring 

Ideally, you’ll have:

  • Software development experience in a regulated industry using TypeScript, with a track record of designing and building complex solutions to customer problems

  • Experience architecting solutions on AWS, knowing which technologies to use when and the trade-offs involved

  • Confidence working with and explaining event-driven architectures and asynchronous APIs

  • Experience in a commercial or client-facing technical role, ideally selling SaaS in a regulated industry, with examples of adapting a solution to meet a customer’s unique needs

  • The ability to distil complex concepts into clear, simple points, and to work through differing opinions with empathy

  • Comfort working autonomously across multiple opportunities, handling ambiguity and knowing which data to use to measure success

An interest in renewable energy and the challenges facing energy retailers will help you hit the ground running.

Tech stack: TypeScript, AWS, event-driven architectures, asynchronous APIs


Our Values

Five values guide how we work at Kaluza:

  • Play to win: Collective pride in decarbonising energy at scale.

  • Solve the real problem: Cutting through complexity to focus on real-world outcomes.

  • Build trust every day: Consistency, transparency and doing what we say.

  • Own the outcome: Full accountability, wins and setbacks, without ego.

  • Go further together: Collaboration, respect and different perspectives.


Our Perks

  • Time off and family: 26 days’ holiday, plus 26 weeks’ full pay for new parents with no qualifying service period

  • Health and security: Private medical insurance with virtual GP, life assurance, pension scheme, free mortgage advice and eye tests

  • Pay and flexibility: Discretionary bonus, a Flex Fund of 5% [of salary] to spend on the benefits you want most, retail discounts through Perks at Work

  • Growth and setup: Personal learning budget, home office budget

  • Climate: Furthr, our climate action app


Come as you are

We want to meet people from all walks of life. The more inclusive we are, the better our work will be, and we recognise talent on merit and potential. If you’re excited about the role but don’t tick every box, we’d still love to hear from you.

Find out more on our careers page and LinkedIn. Our Applicant Data Protection Policy is here.

title: Principal Cloud Engineer

About the job

Build the cloud platform that powers Graphcore’s next generation AI systems.

As a Principal Cloud Engineer, you will help develop, deploy and operate cloud services across Graphcore’s AI infrastructure. You will work on private and public cloud systems used by internal teams and customers.

Your work will shape how high-performance AI systems are integrated, validated, benchmarked and optimised. You will help keep complex infrastructure reliable, observable and ready for demanding workloads.

You will own significant technical initiatives, from OpenStack-based services to Infrastructure-as-Code automation. You will also mentor engineers and turn user needs into services that perform at scale.

This role puts you close to pre-release hardware, advanced systems and real product challenges.

The Cloud Platform Team sits within Software Platform and works closely with Software Platform, Datacentre Operations and Product Development. The team builds systems for internal users and customers, often using new components before they are proven.

Work moves through practical engineering, clear ownership and fast feedback from users. You will be expected to take responsibility, speak up early and lead critical infrastructure work without close oversight.

Decisions are grounded in evidence from benchmarks, observability data and operational performance. The team values engineers who can think big, act fast and bring others with them.

What we’re looking for

  • Strong infrastructure or IT background, with private-cloud or on-premises cloud experience.

  • Hands-on experience with Infrastructure-as-Code tools such as Terraform/OpenTofu, Ansible or Packer.
  • Experience with CI or testing pipelines, version control and cloud service deployment.

title: Principal Product Designer: UX/UI
descriptionHtml:
About Us

At algo1, we are reinventing one of the world’s most familiar experiences: the in-store grocery trip. We are building an AI-native product that understands each shopper, responds to their context in real time and makes an everyday experience less stressful, more personal and more engaging.

We’re backed by leading investors and founded by two entrepreneurs: one with a track record of building companies, and the other a recognised leader in data and shopper analytics. Together, they have built a team of frontier AI researchers and engineers, product and strategy leaders, and senior operators from major UK and US grocery businesses.

The people who join now will have an opportunity to shape the product, the culture, and what algo1 becomes.

The Role

You'll report to our Head of Design, who sets the overall design direction across our consumer and business applications, brand and website. You'll be our most senior hands-on product designer, owning the UX, UI and design system of our consumer applications, with significant influence over product direction.

We're building something with no established design playbook: a consumer experience that connects the digital and physical worlds of grocery shopping. The challenge is that a store isn't a website. Shoppers are moving, browsing shelves and making decisions in seconds. The store must remain the main event, with our technology playing a supporting role rather than competing for attention.

The hardest part is making this feel intuitive for everyone, from digitally confident shoppers to people who rarely use technology in stores. You'll need exceptional consumer mobile design skills, the curiosity to rethink familiar interaction patterns and the judgement to make sophisticated AI feel effortless.

You'll work closely with product, engineering and machine learning to shape what we build, not just how it looks. You'll have the opportunity to test your ideas with real shoppers, improve existing experiences and invent new ones as we build towards scale. Success will be measured by how much easier and more engaging you make shopping, not by how many screens you design.

This is a senior individual contributor role. You won't manage people initially, but you'll help hire and mentor the designers who join next, set the quality bar and establish how the team works.

How you work matters as much as what you design. We're agentic-first and everyone has access to max-tier AI tools, so you'll never be rate-limited. You'll use AI throughout the design process, from exploration and prototyping to design-to-code and QA, and help us discover better ways to build.

What You'll Own

  • Consumer UX and UI. Own the quality of our mobile consumer experience, from complex journeys and interaction patterns to clear, polished, production-ready screens. Make every interaction feel simple, intuitive and consistent.

  • Connected shopper journeys. Design experiences that move naturally between home and store. Bring digital discovery, planning and personalisation into physical shopping without distracting from the products on the shelves.

  • Product thinking and innovation. Work with product and engineering to define problems, challenge assumptions and shape the roadmap. Invent new interaction patterns where conventional mobile UX doesn't translate to the physical world.

  • The design system. Own the components, tokens, patterns and documentation that keep our consumer experience consistent as we scale. Keep Figma and code aligned, manage contributions and prevent design drift.

  • Shopper research and measurable improvement. Observe and test with real shoppers across different ages, abilities and levels of digital confidence. Use usability testing, product analytics and UX audits to identify friction, prioritise improvements and measure engagement and task success.

  • AI interaction quality. Design how AI behaves within the shopping experience: when it helps, how it communicates and when it stays out of the way. Make intelligent features understandable, useful and always under the shopper's control.

  • Raise the design bar. Lead design QA, accessibility reviews and critique. Establish effective AI-native design workflows, mentor other designers and make sure what ships meets the quality bar.

About You

Must Have

  • Exceptional consumer mobile design. You've led UX and UI design for a high-quality, complex consumer mobile product. Your portfolio demonstrates outstanding visual and interaction craft, including excellent hierarchy, layout, typography and attention to detail, alongside strong product thinking and measurable improvements to real user experiences.

  • First-principles thinker. You challenge established UX conventions, simplify complex problems and can invent new interaction patterns when existing ones don't work. You're comfortable balancing innovation with familiarity and ease of use.

  • Design-system ownership. You've maintained and evolved a design system in production, working closely with engineering on components, tokens, documentation, consistency and adoption.

  • Evidence-led product thinking. You combine user research, usability testing, accessibility principles and product analytics to make better decisions. You can demonstrate how your work improved usability, engagement or other meaningful outcomes.

  • Technical fluency. You understand modern design-to-code workflows and work effectively with front-end engineers to ensure the experience that ships matches the design intent.

  • AI-native mindset. You actively use AI tools throughout your design process, experiment with new ways of working and know where human judgement and craft remain essential.

  • High agency and ownership. You take responsibility from problem definition through to shipped experience, influence product decisions and maintain exceptional standards in a fast-moving environment.

Nice to Have

  • Physical-world experiences. Experience designing for retail, in-store screens, kiosks, connected devices or products that bridge digital and physical environments.

  • Front-end development. HTML, CSS or React skills, with the ability to contribute directly to a coded design system.

  • Product analytics. Experience with funnels, session recordings, experimentation and A/B testing.

  • Motion and interaction design. The ability to use motion, transitions and feedback to make interfaces more intuitive.

  • Early-stage startup experience. You've helped build a product or design practice while the company and team were growing.

How We Work

We’re a startup, so this is a high-intensity environment. The people who thrive here are curious, proactive, and love building. If you’re happiest when you’re creating, experimenting, and moving fast, you’ll fit right in.

We draw our energy from being together, so this is primarily an office-based role. It suits someone who enjoys the quick conversations and shared momentum that comes from building together. Our office is on what we think is the best garden square in London, just a couple of minutes from Tottenham Court Road, so it's easy to get to and a great place to be.

What We Offer

  • Competitive salary and meaningful equity.

  • 25 days’ annual leave.

  • The opportunity to shape a new consumer experience with the potential to reach millions of shoppers.

title: Principal Software Engineer, Frontend Experiences
descriptionHtml:
Algolia is the retrieval intelligence layer that turns intent into trusted, decision-grade outcomes. Powering more than 1.7 trillion queries a year for over 18,000 customers with millisecond latency and 99.999% reliability, we are the recognized leader for Search and Product Discovery by top industry analyst firms. The Algolia platform turns a company's products, content, and business rules into data that humans, applications and AI agents can act upon. The result is trusted customer experiences with stronger conversions for measurable business impact.  

If you're a problem solver, able to think outside the box and eager to nurture others and learn from them, then this is your challenge!


As a principal engineer working across the entire frontend stack, from design-system primitives to product-level architecture, you will shape how developers build with Algolia and how customers experience our products.

In the Frontend Experiences team, we're on a mission to make it effortless for developers to build great search and discovery experiences on the front end, with libraries, components and tooling that are fast, accessible, and a pleasure to use. Our work reaches customers and their end users directly, on the web and on mobile, so the quality bar is high and the feedback loop is short.


Right now, that includes a cross-team, multi-quarter effort to evolve the Algolia Dashboard from a collection of product surfaces into one coherent environment: a new navigation and information architecture, a shared component foundation, and an interaction model that supports traditional configuration, conversational assistance and agentic workflows side by side.


The team is looking for an experienced individual who is well versed in defining, building and operating scalable architectures, with proven strengths in cross-team collaboration, taking solutions all the way through delivery to adoption by other engineering teams and by customers. You will play a pivotal role in architecting and implementing systems that play a central role across all of Algolia's front-end products, including libraries that run in production on thousands of customer sites. You will also play a role in training/mentoring and leading team members.


YOUR ROLE WILL CONSIST OF:


  • Defining the multi-year technical vision for Algolia's front-end platform, and turning it into roadmaps and projects that several teams can execute;
  • Playing an active role in the evolution of the Algolia Dashboard: shaping the experience architecture, the component strategy and the technical foundations for conversational and agentic UX, and partnering with engineering, product and design leadership to sequence delivery;
  • Driving convergence on a shared component library, reducing duplicated components and inconsistent patterns across product surfaces;
  • Designing and delivering solutions that will scale with significant volumes, be highly available, performant and resilient, including on pages and apps we do not control;
  • Owning solutions, taking them all the way through delivery to adoption by engineering teams and customers;
  • Shaping API design, versioning and backward-compatibility strategy for public libraries used by a large developer community;
  • Embodying technical expertise, that the team can refer to for advice or validation of a solution;
  • Setting engineering standards and best practices to be followed by engineers

YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF YOU HAVE:


  • Excellent communication and organization skills
  • 10+ years of experience, with a track record of setting technical direction across multiple teams
  • Experience as a thought leader/standard-bearer for engineers, inside and outside the company (talks, open source, writing)
  • Proven experience leading engineers on large, cross-cutting projects
  • Extensive experience designing full stack solutions, interacting with microservice architectures, and strong grounding beyond the frontend (APIs, backend services, delivery infrastructure) to make sound end-to-end trade-offs
  • Deep frontend expertise (TypeScript, modern web platform, React and other major frameworks, accessibility, bundle size and runtime performance)
  • Experience designing and maintaining public libraries, SDKs or design systems, with a feel for API ergonomics and a track record of managing breaking changes
  • Experience building complex, high traffic & multi products web applications such as dashboards or admin consoles, and leading cross-team UI consolidation efforts
  • Interest in conversational and agentic interfaces (chat, streaming responses, tool-driven workflows) and in the architecture needed to support them
  • Familiarity with search UX patterns and with generative AI and agentic experiences is a plus
  • Preference for candidates with experience at our current stage and beyond (over 10,000 customers, $50-200M ARR range, high growth, lots of change and building internal infrastructure).

Algolia does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, military status, veteran status, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law.

The annual base salary compensation range for this role reflects market pay data within this location. The exact compensation offered for this role may vary depending on specific location and job-related knowledge, technical skills, and experience; and is only one part of our Total Rewards philosophy to compensate and recognize employees for their work.

Base Salary Pay Range€108.000—€135.000 EUR

FLEXIBLE WORKPLACE STRATEGY:

Algolia’s flexible workplace model is designed to empower all Algolians to fulfill our mission to power search and discovery with ease. We place an emphasis on an individual’s impact, contribution, and output, over their physical location. Algolia is a high-trust environment and many of our team members have the autonomy to choose where they want to work and when. 

We have a global presence with offices in Paris, NYC, London, Sydney and Bucharest, however we also offer many of our team members the option to work remotely either as fully remote or hybrid-remote employees. Positions listed as "Remote" are only available for remote work within the specified country. Positions listed within a specific city are only available in that location - depending on the role it may be available with either a hybrid-remote or in-office schedule.

WE’RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO CAN LIVE OUR VALUES:

  • GRIT - Problem-solving and perseverance capability in an ever-changing and growing environment.
  • TRUST - Willingness to trust our co-workers and to take ownership.
  • CANDOR - Ability to receive and give constructive feedback.
  • CARE - Genuine care about other team members, our clients and the decisions we make in the company.
  • HUMILITY - Aptitude for learning from others, putting ego aside.

We’re looking for talented, passionate people to help build the world’s best search and discovery technology. We value autonomy, diversity, and collaboration. We’re committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone is respected and supported—regardless of race, age, ancestry, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, color, veteran status, disability, or socioeconomic background.

IMPORTANT NOTICE FOR CANDIDATES - Recruitment Fraud Notice

We’ve recently seen an increase in recruitment scams targeting job seekers. To help protect yourself, please keep the following in mind:

READY TO APPLY?

title: Product Manager – Agent Experience ( Français/ Anglais)
descriptionHtml:
Product Manager – Agent Experience

Lieu : Paris de préférence, possibilité à Londres (hybride, trois jours par semaine au bureau)
Équipe : Customer Care
Langues : Maîtrise du français et de l’anglais
Contrat : CDI
Rattachement : Lead Product Manager

À noter : ce poste est ouvert à Paris et à Londres, et nécessite un droit de travailler déjà acquis dans le pays où vous serez basé(e) (UE pour Paris, Royaume-Uni pour Londres). Nous ne pouvons pas proposer de parrainage de visa, mais nous étudions le parrainage poste par poste : gardez un œil sur notre site carrières pour de futures opportunités.

Merci de soumettre votre CV en anglais.

À propos de Kaluza

Kaluza est la plateforme d’Energy Intelligence qui transforme la complexité de l’énergie en coordination fluide. Nous aidons les énergéticiens à relever les défis d’aujourd’hui tout en accélérant la transition vers un avenir propre et électrifié.

Notre plateforme orchestre des millions de décisions en temps réel entre les foyers, les appareils, les marchés et les réseaux. En associant algorithmes prédictifs et conception centrée sur l’humain, Kaluza rend l’énergie propre fiable, abordable et adaptée à la vie de tous les jours.

Avec des équipes en Europe, en Asie et en Australie, et une joint-venture avec Mitsubishi Corporation au Japon, nous accompagnons des acteurs majeurs comme OVO, AGL et ENGIE, ainsi que des entreprises innovantes comme Volvo et Volkswagen.

Ce que vous ferez

  • Piloter la roadmap : porter la stratégie de bout en bout de Kaluza Agent Experience (KAE) sur le marché européen, en cohérence avec les objectifs produit globaux et affinée par les besoins clients locaux et les comportements des agents. Vous suivrez les indicateurs opérationnels clés (AHT, FCR, CSAT, adoption de l’IA, onboarding) pour vous assurer que chaque évolution améliore l’expérience des agents et des clients.

  • Concevoir les parcours et garantir la cohérence UX : être le garant de l’expérience agent sur l’ensemble de KAE. Vous travaillerez avec les équipes UX et métier pour appliquer des patterns communs, réduire la charge cognitive des agents et rester aligné avec le design system, y compris quand de nouvelles capacités d’automatisation et d’assistance par l’IA sont introduites.

  • Mener les intégrations et l’onboarding client : piloter les intégrations techniques et produit avec des plateformes tierces, et superviser de bout en bout le déploiement de nouvelles instances KAE pour les nouveaux clients, de la phase de découverte jusqu’à la mise en production.

  • Garantir l’accessibilité et la conformité : défendre les réglementations européennes d’accessibilité dès la conception, en traduisant les exigences réglementaires et spécifiques à chaque marché en besoins techniques concrets.

  • Accompagner les clients et créer de la valeur : être l’expert de confiance des clients sur l’expérience agent, en défendant une configuration native de la plateforme plutôt que des développements sur mesure.

  • Rester les mains dans le cambouis, de la livraison à l’accompagnement : vous impliquer sur l’ensemble du cycle de vie du développement produit (PDLC), des sessions de discovery avec les agents aux boucles de feedback, et produire les supports qui favorisent l’adoption côté clients.

(À noter : des déplacements chez les clients, par exemple à Bruxelles, sont à prévoir, environ 1 à 3 par mois au début, puis 1 à 2 par trimestre.)

Ce que vous apporterez

Idéalement, vous avez :

  • Une expertise centres de contact et UX : une solide expérience de la responsabilité de parcours utilisateurs de bout en bout pour des outils opérationnels très sollicités (par exemple des postes de travail d’agents), avec une vraie pratique de la recherche utilisateur, de la cartographie de parcours et des tests d’usabilité auprès d’agents et de superviseurs.

  • Une connaissance de l’accessibilité européenne et de l’intégration de plateformes : une bonne maîtrise des standards d’accessibilité européens, ainsi qu’une expérience avérée d’intégration de produits avec des plateformes tierces et des écosystèmes de fournisseurs complexes.

  • Une expérience de delivery client et d’expansion de marché : un historique de mise en œuvre ou de localisation d’un produit pour des clients entreprise externes, en menant les solutions de zéro à la mise en production : discovery, configuration et conduite du changement.

  • Un jugement fondé sur la donnée et de l’influence : la capacité démontrée à vous appuyer sur des indicateurs opérationnels (AHT, FCR, CSAT, effort de l’agent) pour défendre vos décisions produit, avec un état d’esprit « plateforme d’abord » qui privilégie les capacités existantes au code sur mesure.

  • Un bilinguisme professionnel : une maîtrise complète, à l’écrit comme à l’oral, du français et de l’anglais.

Ce qui fera la différence

  • Une expérience de l’utilisation d’outils d’IA, de capacités de machine learning ou d’intégrations LLM dans des workflows produit, pour renforcer l’intelligence de la plateforme et l’automatisation directement dans les environnements de poste de travail du service client.

  • Une expérience dans des plateformes SaaS, le secteur de l’énergie ou des migrations d’envergure chez des opérateurs de services publics.

  • Une expérience concrète de la mise à l’échelle de la cohérence UI entre plusieurs équipes produit.

Où vous travaillerez

Nous proposons un cadre de travail flexible, avec trois jours par semaine au bureau. C’est le meilleur des deux mondes : du temps réel ensemble pour collaborer et créer des liens, et la liberté de travailler comme vous le préférez le reste de la semaine.

Nos valeurs

Cinq valeurs guident notre façon de travailler chez Kaluza :

  • Jouer pour gagner : la fierté collective de décarboner l’énergie à grande échelle.

  • Résoudre le vrai problème : aller droit au but pour se concentrer sur des résultats concrets.

  • Bâtir la confiance chaque jour : constance, transparence et tenir parole.

  • Assumer les résultats : une responsabilité totale, dans les succès comme dans les échecs, sans ego.

  • Aller plus loin ensemble : collaboration, respect et diversité de points de vue.

Nos avantages

  • Financier et assurances : bonus discrétionnaire, mutuelle santé Alan, assurance décès et invalidité (prévoyance) x3 via Alan, et cotisations de Sécurité sociale standard (retraite, allocations familiales, assurance chômage)

  • Indemnités : remboursement de 50 % des frais de transport, indemnité télétravail de 200 € et budget formation de 150 €

  • Congés et flexibilité : 25 jours de congés + jours fériés + jours de RTT, congé « Moments Qui Comptent », congé de compassion, deux jours de bénévolat rémunérés, travail flexible et possibilité de congé sabbatique

Venez comme vous êtes

title: Product Manager
descriptionHtml:
Weekly office requirement: Monday/Wednesday weekly
Employment type: Permanent
Seniority level: Mid-senior

At GWI we’re always looking for extraordinary people who thrive on making an extraordinary impact. Right now we’re looking for a Product Manager to play a key role in our User Management (Revenue & Enablement) team in London. If that’s you, and making a difference gets you out of bed in the morning, keep reading. It could be the start of something, well, extraordinary.


Sounds great, what will I be doing? 🤔

As our Product Manager you'll own the systems that make GWI's subscription and consumption business run, such as billing, metering, user plans, feature access, product analytics and user messaging. It's the layer everything else sits on. Get it right and GWI can price, package and sell in new ways.


Two big pieces of work sit at the heart of this role. The first is billing for our consumption products, which is an area we're actively developing, and one you'll help shape. The second is making our internal tools talk to each other properly, so user data flows consistently between them and Salesforce, and everyone across the business is working from the same picture. Most of your stakeholders are internal - Revenue Operations, Finance, Business Intelligence, Client Success and Engineering - with some direct client contact along the way. You'll lead one squad of front-end and back-end engineers and a designer, alongside the PM and Engineers in our sister squad, Identity & Access - together you cover the whole of User Management.


A few things you’ll be responsible for: 


👉 Connecting our internal user management tools with Salesforce and each other, so data flows consistently and user information is mapped the same way everywhere

👉 Billing for our consumption products - metering, API usage, payment flows and user plans

👉 Customer feature flags, access and management - who can see what, and why

👉 Product analytics - event firing, sign-up flow data, usage data - so the business can see what's happening and act on it

👉 Building the roadmap from client feedback, internal stakeholder input and usage analytics, and prioritising the most valuable work

👉 Scoping the work and owning how your squad delivers it

It’s also fun; shaking things up is what working for GWI is all about. You’ll need to be flexible, comfortable with continuous change, and working in a high-tempo environment.


What do I need to bring with me? 🧳

You’ll need to be able to demonstrate the core skills this role requires. You don't have to tick all the boxes right away; the important thing is that you’re willing to learn. Here’s what the team will be looking for in you:


👉 You've shipped products at a B2B company

👉 You've built complex roadmaps with cross-functional dependencies, and you can balance multiple priorities without losing the plot

👉 You make informed decisions at pace, even when the picture isn't complete

👉 You're a strong problem solver, negotiator and influencer — you get alignment without needing authority

👉 You explain complex things clearly to very different audiences: execs, engineers, customers

👉 You ask questions and draw knowledge out of your team to find the right engineering and design solutions

👉 You make informed decisions at pace, even when the picture isn't complete, and you're happy taking a big initiative and running with it

👉 Bonus points if you've worked with Salesforce before, or with tools that need to sync data between systems and internal user management systems.


Equally important is attitude. We want people who think big (to make an impact), ask why (to find a better way), and show respect (to everyone, at every level, all the time). Those are our values, and they’re a big part of what we’re looking for in you.


Why Join Us

👉 You'll work on how GWI packages its consumption products - commercial problems with real weight behind them

👉 Your squad owns infrastructure the whole company depends on, so the work gets noticed

👉 You'll build relationships across the business, from Finance to Engineering to the Exec team

👉 You'll learn from a senior PM who knows this space, with room to run your own squad your way

As a Disability Confident employer, we welcome applications from disabled candidates and are committed to making adjustments throughout the hiring process—whether that's extra time, materials in advance or a different format, breaks, an adjusted interview format, assistive tools, or flexible scheduling. We're happy to discuss whatever would work best for you.

We actively encourage applications from underrepresented and marginalised communities.

At GWI, you'll find a place to contribute meaningfully, grow professionally, and belong fully.

title: Product Manager, New Product Bet (Principal-level)
descriptionHtml:
Synthesia is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US.

As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations.

Following our recent Series E funding round, where we raised $200 million, our valuation stands at $4 billion. Our total funding exceeds $530 million from premier investors including Accel, NVentures (Nvidia's VC arm), Kleiner Perkins, GV, and Evantic Capital, alongside the founders and operators of Stripe, Datadog, Miro, and Webflow.

About the role

Almost any company can produce training video at scale today. Almost none can tell you whether it actually made someone better at their job. We're building the product that closes that gap: an agentic, real-time experience where people practice live, dynamic scenarios, and where organizations finally get genuine signal on readiness, instead of a metric tied to course completion. This is a zero-to-one bet on what comes after content, which is practice, and proof.

You'll own one of two of the domains inside that bet, Surveys and Guidance, from strategy through ship.

Why now

Real-time, agentic AI has only just become good enough to hold a convincing live scenario, and to make sense of what happens inside one. The window to define this category is open now, and we intend to own it.

The problem you're solving

Today, the most a company can do to check whether someone has genuinely learned something is watch them complete a module or pass a quiz. The behaviors that matter in real roles, in real moments, are rarely tested reliably, and what comes back to the business is a thin, lagging signal.

We have the underlying technology to change that. What we need is a product manager who can turn it into something an enterprise will use to prepare its people, and that an end user actually wants to engage with, across two connected domains:

  • Surveys - capturing structured, trustworthy signal at scale: how people feel, how they're performing, and where the gaps are.

  • Guidance - giving people direction in the moment they need it, live and in context, rather than as a debrief after the fact.

Both sit inside the same bet: give organizations proof of readiness, not just proof of attendance.

What you'll be doing

  • Owning the multi-quarter strategy for Surveys and Guidance, setting the direction, identifying the right problems to solve, and making the trade-offs needed to deliver against them.

  • Defining and evolving the success metrics for both domains, and connecting product outcomes directly to commercial results: retention, expansion, and revenue impact.

  • Getting close to the customers who matter most: understanding how they think, where current tools leave them exposed, and translating that into a product direction others can act on.

  • Driving a shared understanding of where these product areas are going and why. Engineering, design, R&D, and commercial counterparts should all be able to articulate the strategy and the reasoning behind it.

  • Producing written narratives, strategy docs, and PRDs, that move decisions forward and give your team the context to build the right thing without a follow-up conversation.

  • Balancing short-term delivery with long-term product health: scoping to reflect execution risk, hitting milestones predictably, and iterating based on evidence rather than opinion.

  • Contributing to improvements in product practice across the team, and actively participating in PM hiring.

Who you are

You've owned a critical product domain before, one where the stakes were real and the strategy was yours to set, not just execute. You're comfortable operating with autonomy on the what, not just the how, and you have a track record of connecting product decisions to commercial outcomes.

You understand that zero-to-one products in complex domains require you to hold two things at once: the discipline to deliver predictably in the short term, and the judgment to make the right long-term bets while the evidence is still forming. You don't wait for a clean brief. You identify the right problems, form a view, and bring others along.

You're a strong written communicator. Engineering and design partners, commercial leads, and senior leadership should all come away from your docs and updates with a clear understanding of where the domain is going and why, without needing to ask.

You care about the quality of the experience. Real-time, agentic products are unforgiving, and you hold a high bar for what "good" feels like, for the user in the moment and for the customer looking at outcomes.

You may be a good fit if you bring

  • Significant experience in product management, with direct experience owning a critical product domain: setting strategy, not just executing it.

  • A track record of connecting product outcomes to commercial results: ARR, retention, expansion, or equivalent.

  • Experience with zero-to-one product development in a complex, experience-driven space. You've navigated the ambiguity of a zero-to-one build and have the scar tissue to show for it.

  • Experience building agentic or AI-powered products. You understand what makes real-time AI interactions feel natural, and what breaks them.

  • Strong written communication: strategy docs, PRDs, and decision memos that others can act on without a follow-up conversation.

  • Experience working alongside enterprise buying motions. You'll be close to the commercial team, and that context matters.

We encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every point above. Strong candidates rarely match a list exactly, and we'd rather hear from you.

Location

Flexible, hybrid role based from our London office.

Our culture

At Synthesia we’re passionate about building, not talking, planning or politicising. We strive to hire the smartest, kindest and most unrelenting people and let them do their best work without distractions. Our work principles serve as our charter for how we make decisions, give feedback and structure our work to empower everyone to go as fast as possible. You can find out more about these principles here.
